recent_posts.title: AI-assisted engineering: Q1 2026 impact report
recent_posts.summary: A quarterly benchmark report from 400+ companies on AI adoption in engineering, covering Q1 2026 data. Key findings: AI adoption has reached 93% industry-wide; engineering managers are now shipping 4x more code than six months ago as agentic tools lower context-switching barriers; junior engineers now save slightly more time with AI (4.9 hrs/week) than Staff+ engineers (4.8 hrs/week), reversing last quarter's trend. The full report also covers Rust-specific AI time savings improvements, quality volatility risks including rising change failure rates, shadow AI risks from developers bypassing enterprise guardrails, and efficiency differences between small and large enterprises.

recent_posts.title: Developer ramp-up time continues to accelerate with AI
recent_posts.summary: New data from a sample of 400 companies shows developer onboarding time, measured by Time to 10th PR, has dropped to an average of 33 days as of early 2026, down from 39 days in Q4 2025 and more than 50% lower than pre-AI baselines in Q1 2024. The improvement is attributed to AI becoming a standard, guided practice in many organizations rather than an individual choice. Developers now use AI to understand codebases, explain architectural decisions, and draft changes for review, shortening the 'figuring things out' phase. The post notes that Time to 10th PR is a narrow metric and does not capture code quality, rework rates, or depth of understanding, which will be explored in future analyses.

recent_posts.title: Measuring AI impact, assessing readiness, and new data trends
recent_posts.summary: A podcast episode exploring how AI is reshaping the entire software development lifecycle beyond just code generation. Key themes include: AI readiness as a developer experience problem (documentation, environments, feedback loops matter more than tool choice), the challenge of measuring AI ROI due to correlation vs. causation issues, two distinct impact buckets (amplification of human productivity vs. augmentation via autonomous agents), and how background agents shift bottlenecks from code production to human review and orchestration. Documentation is highlighted as becoming critical infrastructure for both human and AI productivity.

recent_posts.title: Introducing DX Annual
recent_posts.summary: DX is launching DX Annual, a conference for developer productivity leaders scheduled for April 16th in San Francisco. The event will host approximately 400 senior engineering leaders from major companies to discuss applying AI across the SDLC, scaling best practices, and evolving DevProd team roles. The conference format includes keynotes, fireside chats, and roundtables with emphasis on peer networking.

recent_posts.title: Using AI to accelerate hiring and productivity at Zapier
recent_posts.summary: Zapier built hundreds of internal AI agents to automate operational tasks like standups, onboarding, and Slack workflows, reducing engineering friction by 10-15%. Rather than cutting headcount, they used AI to increase engineer productivity and value per hire, making additional hiring more attractive. Their approach focuses on removing coordination overhead through lightweight agents that work together, with new automations taking days to deploy. The strategy demonstrates how AI can augment teams by eliminating administrative work, allowing engineers to focus on core development tasks.

recent_posts.title: DORA’s 2025 research on the impact of AI
recent_posts.summary: DORA's 2025 research reveals that traditional delivery metrics cannot capture AI's true impact on engineering systems. AI acts as an organizational amplifier, accelerating healthy practices while intensifying existing bottlenecks. The research introduces five software delivery performance metrics and the DORA AI Capabilities Model, emphasizing that successful AI adoption depends on team capabilities rather than tool selection. Key findings show AI shifts bottlenecks downstream to code review, junior engineers adopt AI more heavily than seniors, and measuring ROI requires qualitative insights beyond dashboards. Leaders need clear AI policies, accessible documentation, and direct conversations with engineers to understand where AI creates friction or value.

recent_posts.title: Do newer AI-native IDEs outperform other AI coding assistants?
recent_posts.summary: Analysis of Q4 2025 data from 400+ companies reveals that AI-native IDEs like Cursor and Claude Code correlate with higher pull request throughput compared to other AI coding assistants. However, organizational factors significantly influence these metrics: smaller companies (under 500 engineers) show higher PR merge rates regardless of tool choice, while enterprise adoption patterns differ—Windsurf gains traction in large organizations while Cursor dominates smaller teams. The data suggests that organizational context, company size, and existing processes play crucial roles in AI tool effectiveness, making comprehensive longitudinal measurement more valuable than single metrics for evaluating AI coding assistant impact.

recent_posts.title: The AI Strategy Playbook: What engineering leaders need to know about driving AI impact
recent_posts.summary: Engineering leaders can drive significant AI productivity gains by prioritizing psychological safety, implementing structured enablement programs, and measuring impact through a mixed-methods framework. Successful AI adoption requires positioning tools as performance multipliers rather than replacements, investing in education and controlled pilots before scaling, and focusing on automation across the entire SDLC beyond just code generation. Teams with strong leadership strategy see major velocity improvements while others experience stalled adoption or confusion.

recent_posts.title: Meetings and interruptions are still the biggest obstacles for developers, even with AI
recent_posts.summary: Research analyzing 130,000+ data points reveals that despite AI saving developers an average of 3.35 hours weekly, traditional productivity bottlenecks like meetings, interruptions, code comprehension, and development environment issues cause significantly greater time losses. While AI agents can address some bottlenecks through automated code reviews, documentation, and knowledge base integration, engineering leaders should first measure their organization's specific friction points before deciding whether AI or process improvements offer the best solution.

recent_posts.title: The evolving role of DevProd teams in the AI era
recent_posts.summary: Platform and DevProd teams are expanding their responsibilities in the AI era, moving beyond traditional CI/CD to include AI tool evaluation, rollout, and measurement. Key focus areas include hardening systems to handle AI-generated code throughput, standardizing AI workflows across organizations, applying AI at scale for technical debt reduction and code migrations, and maintaining strong measurement frameworks to track AI impact beyond simple metrics like lines of code.
